hook.text: Every year, 24 billion tons of topsoil wash away globally. That's enough to fill 160 million train cars.

buildup.text: Raindrops hit bare soil at 20 mph, dislodging particles. Sheet flow carries them downhill.

discovery.text: Rills form first—tiny channels. Left unchecked, they become gullies that carve permanent scars in fields.

twist.text: Cover crops and mulch absorb raindrop impact. A simple plant cover stops most erosion before it starts.

climax.text: Soil erodes 10 to 100 times faster than it forms. We're spending a savings account we can't refill.

punchline.text: Rain builds soil over centuries. Rain destroys it in hours.

details.summary: Water erosion removes an estimated 36 billion tons of topsoil globally each year through raindrop impact, sheet flow, rill formation, and gullying. This topic covers the mechanics of water erosion, the factors that accelerate it, and conservation practices that prevent it.
details.whyItMatters: Water erosion is the number one threat to global soil resources. It removes the most fertile topsoil first, degrades water quality through sediment and chemical runoff, and costs agriculture an estimated $44 billion annually in the United States.
takeaways: Water erosion removes approximately 36 billion tons of topsoil globally each year
Erosion starts with raindrop splash, progresses to sheet wash, then rills and gullies
Contour farming, terracing, cover crops, and waterways are primary erosion controls

faq.question: How does water erosion physically remove topsoil?
faq.answer: Raindrops strike bare soil at up to 30 km/h, detaching particles and destroying soil aggregates. Sheet flow carries detached particles downslope. As flow concentrates, it cuts rills that can merge into gullies meters deep. Each stage removes progressively more soil irreversibly.

faq.question: What farming practices most effectively prevent water erosion?
faq.answer: Maintaining ground cover (cover crops, mulch, crop residues) protects against raindrop impact. Contour farming and terracing slow water flow. Grassed waterways channel runoff safely. No-till farming preserves surface residue. Buffer strips filter sediment before it reaches waterways.
